metadata.title: SCIENTIFIC CLAIM, THRESHOLD & UNCERTAINTY CALIBRATION AUDIT

part1_uncertainty_calibration_audit.scientific_justification: Uncertainty responsiveness is demonstrated (sigma inflates 2.54x on NMC and 2.88x on UNKNOWN). However, uncertainty calibration cannot be established: (1) Total physical sample size N=12 with shifted NMC N=3 and UNKNOWN N=1 provides zero statistical power for reliability or quantile binning; (2) Pearson correlation between error and sigma across the cohort is r=-0.089 (p=0.78), indicating that inflated sigma is an engineered heuristic penalty rather than an empirically calibrated posterior variance; (3) While 95% nominal empirical coverage is 100% due to aggressive inflation, the interval width expands to 1.99-2.26 SOH units on shifted domains, which exceeds the entire physical [0.0, 1.0] domain, making intervals practically uninformative rather than calibrated.

part2_threshold_sensitivity_audit.origin_of_0_90: Originates from heuristic multi-level gating in ChemistryDisambiguationEngine: P(M|y) >= 0.990 is classified as KNOWN, 0.900 <= P(M|y) < 0.990 as PROBABLE, and P(M|y) < 0.900 as AMBIGUOUS / HOLD_FOR_DIAGNOSTICS. It was chosen as an engineering design constant, NOT from prospective ROC/Youden-J optimization.
part2_threshold_sensitivity_audit.power_limitation: With only N=12 physical cells (8 LFP with conf=0.99, 3 NMC with conf=0.99, 1 UNKNOWN with conf=0.334), all thresholds between 0.50 and 0.95 produce identical binary decisions on the physical cohort (DEFER=1/12, PROCEED=11/12, False Acceptance=0.0). Empirical ROC/PR curve threshold optimization is completely underpowered until continuous confidence distributions from a prospective multi-cell cohort (N >= 30 per chemistry) become available.

part3_model_comparability_and_tradeoff.comparability_notes: All seven models A0 through A6 were evaluated under strictly identical conditions: same 12 physical specimens, same 12 LOBO splits, same evaluation target (true_soh), same random seed, and same missing-value median imputation mechanism. The metrics are DIRECTLY COMPARABLE across models.

a1_vs_a6_tradeoff.safety_gain: Reduces unsupported out-of-distribution false acceptance from 8.33% to 0.00%
a1_vs_a6_tradeoff.scientific_interpretation: Model A6 is NOT more accurate than Model A1. It has a higher average MAE (0.1507 vs 0.1370, +9.98% error). However, Model A1 achieves lower apparent MAE by exploiting raw voltage features (V_MEAN) which fail catastrophically under unmodeled domain shifts and blindly accepts out-of-distribution cells. Model A6 is a RISK-CONSTRAINED, DOMAIN-AWARE model that sacrifices 0.0137 MAE to eliminate unsupported confident acceptance on unmodeled chemistries by deferring when epistemic evidence is insufficient.

DELTA_V_TOTAL.notes: Monotonic association observed across 8 LFP and 3 NMC cells. Full cross-chemistry validation remains unproven.

DELTA_V_OHMIC.notes: Collinear with R0 under fixed 10A current (r=1.0000). Modest independent incremental value (+0.00016 MAE).

R0_OHMIC.notes: R0_OHMIC is a protocol- and operating-condition-dependent electrical observation whose interpretation requires contextual normalization. Under fixed current, r=1.0000 with DELTA_V_OHMIC. Variance reduction (76%) does not demonstrate incremental battery-disjoint prognostic value.

RELAXATION_DELTA_V.notes: Zero incremental value under rapid 10s screening.

V_MEAN.notes: Acts as strong chemistry proxy (d=3.82); pooling across chemistries produces negative transfer.

T_MEAN.notes: Mandatory thermal safety boundary; conditional environmental context for Arrhenius correction.

part5_claim_retraction_audit.subject: Uncertainty Inflation vs Calibration
part5_claim_retraction_audit.historical_text: Overconfident Under Domain Shift: FALSE / Overconfidence successfully eliminated.
part5_claim_retraction_audit.audited_correction: The tested domain-shift scenarios produced increased epistemic uncertainty and DEFER behavior. Calibration of uncertainty against independent physical prediction error remains unvalidated.

part5_claim_retraction_audit.subject: Chemistry Confidence Threshold
part5_claim_retraction_audit.audited_correction: P(M|y) < 0.90 is a provisional engineering threshold, not an empirically calibrated statistical cutoff. The threshold has not been prospectively calibrated against a sufficient physical domain-validation cohort.

part5_claim_retraction_audit.subject: R0_OHMIC Status
part5_claim_retraction_audit.audited_correction: R0_OHMIC is a protocol- and operating-condition-dependent electrical observation whose interpretation requires contextual normalization. Status downgraded to CONTEXTUAL / PROVISIONAL because cross-chemistry variance reduction does not establish incremental battery-disjoint prognostic value.

part5_claim_retraction_audit.subject: Contact Resistance Distinction
part5_claim_retraction_audit.historical_text: DELTA_V_OHMIC can distinguish contact resistance under multi-rate pulses.
part5_claim_retraction_audit.audited_correction: DELTA_V_OHMIC is sensitive to changes in aggregate electrical response under multi-rate pulse conditions. Terminal measurements aggregate bulk ohmic, electrochemical polarization, contact resistance, wiring, and tabs.

part5_claim_retraction_audit.subject: Hardware Comparator Scope
part5_claim_retraction_audit.historical_text: Hardware safety comparator protects against multi-chemistry overvoltage excursions.
part5_claim_retraction_audit.audited_correction: The tested LFP-configured hardware comparator prevented the tested NMC operating condition from proceeding, demonstrating that chemistry-specific hardware thresholds must be validated before cross-chemistry operation.

part5_claim_retraction_audit.subject: Model A3 Normalization Failure
part5_claim_retraction_audit.historical_text: Continuous parameter scaling on small cohorts is mathematically unsound.
part5_claim_retraction_audit.audited_correction: The tested continuous chemistry-conditioned normalization implementation was unstable under the available small-N NMC cohort, with variance estimates becoming numerically unstable.

part5_claim_retraction_audit.subject: DELTA_V_TOTAL Cross-Chemistry Validation
part5_claim_retraction_audit.historical_text: DELTA_V_TOTAL is validated across LFP and NMC.
part5_claim_retraction_audit.audited_correction: DELTA_V_TOTAL exhibited a monotonic association with the available degradation-related observations in both the LFP cohort and the small exploratory NMC cohort. Cross-chemistry generalization remains unproven.

part5_claim_retraction_audit.subject: Chemistry vs Form-Factor Confounding
part5_claim_retraction_audit.historical_text: Domain shift differences are attributed to LFP vs NMC chemistry differences.
part5_claim_retraction_audit.audited_correction: Chemistry and physical/electrical configuration are confounded in the available physical cohort (LFP 4S cylindrical vs NMC single pouch), preventing clean attribution of observed domain differences to chemistry alone.
